# yantra-core

> The orchestration logic for Yantra, with no opinion about who calls it. Reaches machines over the
> system `ssh` binary, opens tmux sessions on them, launches and observes Claude Code, and reads the
> Tailscale inventory. A library: it never prints and never exits (ADR-0005). The CLI calls it
> in-process today; `yantrad` will call the same functions from an HTTP handler.

Every module below has a `//!` header explaining *why* it is shaped the way it is, usually naming the
invariant that forced it. Those headers are the real documentation — the notes here say which file to
open, not what it contains.

## Entry points

Each takes a workspace name — `doctor` a machine name — loads it from
`~/.config/yantra/workspaces/<name>.toml`, and opens an ssh connection. Each also exposes a generic
half taking an `Exec`, which is what the tests drive.

- [up.rs](src/up.rs): open a workspace's tmux session, optionally launching an agent in it. Idempotent — a second call attaches. Returns `Opened::{Created,Attached}`. **On macOS it refuses when no tmux server is running rather than starting one** ([ADR-0018](../../docs/adr/0018-the-tmux-server-carries-the-macos-login-session.md) §1, Y-151): a server started over ssh forks panes that cannot read the login keychain (I-44). The far side's OS arrives as an argument of the generic half, so a container test on Linux drives that branch.
- [resume.rs](src/resume.rs): put the agent back on the conversation it left off, via `claude --continue --fork-session`. Refuses rather than guesses when the pane holds something it did not start. Carries ADR-0018 §1 too, and asks it before the gate rather than leaving it to `up::open` — every plan but one prepares the agent first.
- [logs.rs](src/logs.rs): read the agent's transcript JSONL, projected down to turns. Selection happens on the far side.
- [status.rs](src/status.rs): is the agent running, finished, stopped, crashed or killed. Reads two sources and reports their disagreement rather than resolving it.
- [down.rs](src/down.rs): stop the session, reporting how the agent ended — read *before* the pane that holds the exit status is destroyed.
- [sessions.rs](src/sessions.rs): every tmux session on every machine a workspace names, queried concurrently, partial answers reported rather than failed.
- [attention.rs](src/attention.rs): what GitHub is waiting on you for, behind the `Forge` trait. Runs the `gh` binary, which holds the OAuth token in the machine's keyring, so §B4 is met by construction and no credential enters this process ([R13](../../docs/research/13-dashboard-revamp-and-github.md) §2.2). Five fields are requested and no more. The three failures a caller must tell apart — absent, logged out, unreachable — were **measured** against `gh` 2.96.0 rather than read from a specification, because none exists.
- [doctor.rs](src/doctor.rs): whether a machine can do what Yantra will ask of it — the nine checks in [D2 §3.1](../../docs/design/02-setup.md), each **present, absent or unknown**. A **read**: it installs nothing and starts nothing, including the tmux server the macOS branch asks about (ADR-0018 §1). Every branch answers `unknown` where it could not ask, which is R-23 and the whole shape of the module: *absent* sends a reader to install something and *unknown* sends them to the machine. Two answers are narrower than they look — `heartbeat` is unknown from anything that is not the daemon holding the beats (ADR-0012, Y-044), which `yantrad` fills in for itself on `GET /api/readiness` (Y-168) rather than this module ever answering it, and `provider-auth` discards its output on the far side, because a real `gh auth status` names the account (§B4).
- [edit.rs](src/edit.rs): change a workspace after it exists. `repo` and `startup` are inert until the next `up`; `machine` is where the session lives, so moving it while a session is open there is **refused** rather than performed — and a machine that cannot be asked is refused too, never assumed empty (R-23).

## Primitives

- [ssh.rs](src/ssh.rs): one command on one machine, over the system `ssh` with `ControlMaster`. Sentinel trailer, base64 payload, `-E` to divert ssh's own diagnostics. ADR-0006. Every connection also gets **Yantra's own `known_hosts`** beside the control sockets, with `StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`, so first contact needs nobody to type anything and a *changed* host key is a hard refusal — measured in [tests/ssh_identity.rs](tests/ssh_identity.rs) rather than assumed. Also `os()` — `uname -s` over that envelope, because ADR-0009 leaves no key joining a workspace's `machine` to a Tailscale `MachineInfo` and ADR-0013's heartbeat may not carry one. A `uname` that did not answer is an error, never a default (R-23).
- [tmux.rs](src/tmux.rs): resolve the binary absolutely, create sessions idempotently, list them, read a pane's ending, kill, and wrap a command so the **server** forks it (`run_shell`, ADR-0018 §5). The densest invariant surface in the crate.
- [agent.rs](src/agent.rs): find `claude`, check the credential, build the launch command, read the running-agent registry. **On macOS the check runs through `tmux run-shell` in the server that will fork the agent** (ADR-0018 §5, Y-151), because the answer depends on which process asks — over ssh it is a `Background` process and answers `loggedIn: false` there forever (I-44). What a pass claims stays bounded by **I-53**: a credential was found, never that it works. Claude Code only, per the one-agent-first guardrail. Its `CANDIDATES` is public because `yantra-agent`'s label probe searches the same directories for the same reason (I-34), and so is `locate` — the probe itself, which [doctor.rs](src/doctor.rs) points at `gh` and `glab`. It takes a `&'static str`, because the name is interpolated into a remote shell command.
- [identity.rs](src/identity.rs): the ssh identity this account reaches the fleet with (Y-144) — an ed25519 key with **no passphrase**, because `BatchMode=yes` has nowhere to type one and an agent is a login session an appliance does not have, and one `Host` block per machine a workspace names binding that key with `IdentitiesOnly`. Idempotent in both halves: an existing key is kept, because regenerating orphans every `authorized_keys` entry, and a machine the config already names is left exactly as it is — that block is ADR-0009's escape hatch and Yantra is not the authority on what a name means. It writes **no `known_hosts`**: [ssh.rs](src/ssh.rs) already gives every connection its own with `accept-new`. `HostName`, `Port`, `User` and `ProxyJump` are the owner's half of [D2 §2](../../docs/design/02-setup.md)'s boundary, and so is placing the public key. A `machine` that is not one `Host` pattern is **refused before anything is written**: nothing validates that field as an ssh destination (ADR-0009), so a name carrying a newline would write config lines of its own into the file that decides how every connection is made.
- [terminfo.rs](src/terminfo.rs): pass the caller's `TERM` through when the far side knows it, fall back when it does not, install on request.
- [inventory.rs](src/inventory.rs): `tailscale status --json` behind a trait, plus `whois`/`owner` for ADR-0016's live authorisation. Read-only and advisory — it observes machines, it never resolves them (ADR-0009). **I-52**: `whois` and `status` name the same node's identity under different keys (`StableID` vs `ID`, `User` vs `UserID`) and the mismatch parses silently, so they need separate structs.
- [workspace.rs](src/workspace.rs): the TOML schema. `deny_unknown_fields`, because a silently ignored key is the worst kind of bug (ADR-0007). `create` writes one (Y-116's CLI half) and **refuses to overwrite**; it validates neither `machine` nor `repo`, because ADR-0009 has Yantra never resolving a machine and `repo` is a path on the far side that `up` already checks there (Y-081). It does refuse an **empty** `machine`, `repo` or `startup` (Y-119) — an absent `startup` is what means *just a shell*, so a blank one is a command that cannot run rather than a second spelling of absence. **`load` refuses the same three, by asking the same predicate** (Y-137), naming the file, the field and the workspace. **`list` returns a `Listing`** (Y-141): the workspaces that loaded, and every file that did not under its name with its reason, so one broken file costs only itself — the outer `Result` is what is left of the old all-or-nothing rule and is about the directory rather than a file in it. `update` is the counterpart Y-126 added: it rewrites only the fields named, renames the new file over the old one, and knows nothing about sessions — that refusal is [edit.rs](src/edit.rs)'s.
- [pty.rs](src/pty.rs): `attach`'s command run under a pseudo-terminal — bytes out, bytes in, resize, and a `Drop` that detaches without ending the session. The third ssh call shape: `Exec` is one-shot with `RequestTTY=no`, `yantra attach` hands the process over with `execve`, and a browser terminal is neither. Shares `ssh.rs`'s connection options through `Ssh::tty_argv`. **Reconnecting is opening another one** — tmux draws the pane for every client that attaches, so no replay buffer belongs here (Y-132, Q5).
- [heartbeat.rs](src/heartbeat.rs): the seven-field wire type `yantra-agent` sends and `yantrad` reads. `deny_unknown_fields` for the same reason as `workspace`, and a two-variant `Power` so unknown power cannot be expressed (ADR-0013).
- [notify.rs](src/notify.rs): the difference between two consecutive looks at the fleet, and one send (Y-146). `Watch::look` is pure and the whole decision: **the first call returns nothing**, because a daemon that persists nothing has no previous state and must not announce the fleet at every reboot; a machine that could not be asked **keeps** the verdicts it had, because unknown is not changed; a workspace the answering machine no longer lists is dropped. `AwaitingTrust` is the verdict that matters most (I-49) and the only one that is news whatever came before it; everything else is a `Running` that stopped being one — never `NoAgent`, never `Stopped`, and **never a telemetry threshold** (ADR-0013's non-goals). `post` is one attempt over `ureq` on a blocking thread, and a failure is the notification gone. **`Notification` carries a workspace and a verdict and has no field for a machine or a repo**, and `Relay`'s `Debug` is hand-written because the token is a secret (§B4, Q5) and so is the topic in the URL — no error carries either. **The relay is a general publish channel** and the notifier is only its first caller (Y-147, answering Q16): `post` takes a `Message` — a body, and ntfy's `Title` and `Priority` as options — a `Notification` renders into one, and **the body is the caller's**, so nothing here composes a workspace's resolved secret into what leaves. `from_env` builds a `Relay` from `YANTRA_NTFY_URL` and `YANTRA_NTFY_TOKEN` and from nowhere else; an absent URL is no relay and is not an error.
- [snapshot.rs](src/snapshot.rs): what a caller last learned about the fleet and when — machines, workspaces, sessions, agents and readiness. Each class carries its own age; "nobody has looked yet" is `None`, and a look that succeeded can still carry a broken workspace file (Y-141). No clock and no loop — those are the daemon's.

## Decisions that constrain this crate

- [ADR-0005](../../docs/adr/0005-core-logic-in-a-library-crate.md): core logic is a library; binaries stay thin. The source of the never-print rule.
- [ADR-0006](../../docs/adr/0006-ssh-exec-transport.md): why the transport looks over-engineered and is not.
- [ADR-0007](../../docs/adr/0007-workspace-schema-v1.md): the workspace schema, with provisioning as an explicit non-goal.
- [ADR-0009](../../docs/adr/0009-machine-names-are-ssh-destinations.md): a `machine` is an ssh destination; `~/.ssh/config` decides what it means.
- [ADR-0011](../../docs/adr/0011-claude-code-runs-as-a-tui-in-tmux.md): the agent is a TUI in tmux, the transcript is the log, and Yantra sends it no input.
- [ADR-0013](../../docs/adr/0013-the-heartbeat-carries-only-what-placement-scores.md): what a heartbeat carries, why each field earns its place, and why absent power data means AC.

## Optional

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): this crate's invariants — the largest share in the project. The single most useful thing to read before changing anything here.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): the crate's own working rules, including which invariant binds which module.
- [../../tracker.md](../../tracker.md): project state — milestones, open tasks, decisions, risks.
- [tests/common/mod.rs](tests/common/mod.rs): the disposable sshd + tmux container every integration test runs against.
- [tests/manual_macbook.rs](tests/manual_macbook.rs): the `#[ignore]`d checks that need the real MacBook rather than a container — `just test-mac <machine>`. Two need a person at that machine and refuse without one: Y-139's measures whether a transcript keeps advancing while the tmux session is detached (Q12, R-1), and Y-151's asks whether the gate finds a credential inside a GUI-login tmux server where ssh finds none (ADR-0018 §5, I-44). Both need that server started from a GUI login, which is the one thing no container can stand in for.
- [tests/pty.rs](tests/pty.rs): Y-127's spike — ssh connections differing only in how the local end is given a terminal, answering whether `^C` reaches a process in a remote pane — followed by Y-128's tests of [pty.rs](src/pty.rs) itself, in the same container, and Y-132's two: a terminal dropped and another opened is drawn the screen the first one left, including a full-screen application on the alternate screen. It is where I-18 was finally measured; its header says what each arm found.
- [tests/ssh_identity.rs](tests/ssh_identity.rs): Y-144 — the identity [identity.rs](src/identity.rs) prepares, reaching a real sshd **by name alone** through the config it wrote, and `ssh.rs`'s known-hosts half proved rather than assumed. Every connection is made from a keypair generated at test time, with `-F` at that config and `IdentityAgent=none`, and each test first asserts the connection is *refused* — it only works once the generated public key is placed, so nothing of the developer's can be what authenticates. What it cannot prove is that OpenSSH finds the file at all: that path comes from `getpwuid`, not `$HOME`.
- [tests/two_clients.rs](tests/two_clients.rs): Y-131 — two live clients on one tmux window, which is what a second browser tab is. Pins I-54 and falsifies R2's *"the smaller clamps pane size"*; `window-size manual` is measured beside it as the rejected alternative.
